research.headline: GameHorizon Suite: Multi-Horizon Data and Evaluation in Gameplay
research.summary: Modern video games provide a measurable testbed for AI models, combining abilities of visual understanding, instruction decomposition, goal planning, and precise action control over multiple temporal horizons. Existing datasets and benchmarks, however, either cover a narrow range of games, lack language instructions, or rely on high-variance online rollouts. To address these challenges, we introduce GameHorizon, a unified data and evaluation suite that measures gameplay capabilities at different horizons for diverse model families.

research.headline: onPanda: Efficient Annotation of On-Policy Alignment Data for LLMs and Agents via Token-Level Correction
research.summary: We present onPanda, an interactive tool for efficiently annotating LLM alignment data and agent trajectories. onPanda adopts token-level correction as its core interaction: while reading a model response, the annotator locates the first inappropriate token and either picks a substitute from the model's candidate tokens or types the correct text via free-form editing. The system then truncates everything after that position and continues generation from the corrected prefix, repeating this locate-correct-continue loop until a satisfactory response is obtained.

frontier.headline: A thermal microwave bus for neutral atom quantum computing
frontier.summary: High-fidelity two-qubit gates in neutral-atom arrays rely on the Rydberg blockade, which is intrinsically short ranged and requires long range connectivity to be achieved through atom shuttling. We propose a four level architecture, where the typical ground state qubit can be leveraged for its long lifetime and the Rydberg states couple to a microwave cavity, allowing for long range cavity mediated gates. We first find the thermal dependence of two established protocols, the dispersive iSWAP native to the Tavis-Cummings model and the Controlled phase gate generated from driving the cavity.

voices.headline: In Defense of Guilt by Association
voices.summary: Vance and Abdul El-Sayed have very little in common ideologically and seem to like each other even less. As part of a nasty exchange of personal insults last month, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Michigan implied that Vance’s grandfather would disapprove of the vice president’s Indian American wife. In response , Vance called El-Sayed “very, very evil” and warned him to “keep my wife’s name the hell out of your mouth because she’s way out of your league.” Yet even as Vance and El-Sayed are happy to trade schoolyard taunts, they can agree on at least one thing: that guilt by association is a contemptible means of scoring cheap political points.

voices.headline: How to Regulate the Ghosts
voices.summary: Ghostbusters is a movie about friendship and slime and the specific melting point of giant marshmallows—which makes it easy to forget that it’s also a movie about regulation. The catastrophe at its center begins when Walter Peck (William Atherton), a bureaucrat from the Environmental Protection Agency, visits the basement of the Ghostbusters’ headquarters and finds a machine he does not understand. The nerdy scientist Egon Spengler (Harold Ramis) explains that it’s a containment system; shutting it off would be “like dropping a bomb on the city.” Peck doesn’t believe in ghosts, and he sure doesn’t believe in the Ghostbusters, so he orders an electrician to turn the machine off.

voices.headline: The Firebrand
voices.summary: ET on September 20, 2026 A bdul El-Sayed certainly enjoys an argument . Our first interview, in a kebab restaurant in Dearborn, Michigan, spun out into a wide-ranging discussion of America’s Middle East policy, and ended with me saying, reluctantly, “Well, let’s not relitigate the Six-Day War.” El-Sayed is campaigning to be the next Democratic senator from Michigan, but he has also become one of his party’s leading critics of Israel. I had observed that Gaza’s Arab neighbors had shown little desire to help Palestinians escape the humanitarian crisis there; he had retorted that without Israel’s bombing campaign, they wouldn’t need sanctuary in the first place.

voices.headline: The Curious Left-Wing Argument Against New AI Regulations
voices.summary: Updated at 10:10 p.m. ET on September 21, 2026 D onald Trump has reacted to terrifying calls for regulation from inside the AI industry with predictable skepticism— insisting , questionably, that the solution requires nothing more than having a “High IQ” president, and further asserting, even more questionably, that he qualifies as one. A more surprising flank of opposition has arisen from a different source: the populist left, which has suggested that existing regulations would be perfectly adequate to rein in a rogue superintelligence bent on eliminating the human race.
